Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

input.prompt:
I need to find the Markdown processing interface in this repository. Search for:
1. Any interface or trait related to markdown processing/rendering/parsing (e.g. MarkdownProcessor, MarkdownParser, MarkdownRenderer, etc.)
2. Concrete implementations of that interface
3. Where those implementations are constructed/instantiated
4. Which components hold references to the interface

Search breadth: very thorough. Look across the entire codebase for markdown-related interfaces, traits, abstract classes. Check dependency injection, service registration, and constructor patterns. Look in all languages (TypeScript, Rust, Go, etc.).

content.text:
Now I have a complete picture. Here is my report.

---

## Markdown Processing Interface -- Complete Analysis

### 1. The Interface

The primary markdown processing interface is the Go `Service` interface defined in:

**`/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/markdown.go`** (lines 31-55)

```go
type Service interface {
    ExtractAll(content []byte) (*ExtractedData, error)
    ExtractTags(content []byte) ([]string, error)
    ExtractProperties(content []byte) (*storepb.MemoPayload_Property, error)
    RenderMarkdown(content []byte) (string, error)
    RenderHTML(content []byte) (string, error)
    GenerateSnippet(content []byte, maxLength int) (string, error)
    ValidateContent(content []byte) error
    RenameTag(content []byte, oldTag, newTag string) (string, error)
}
```

This interface provides tag/mention extraction, property computation, markdown-to-markdown round-tripping, HTML rendering, snippet generation, content validation, and tag renaming.

### 2. Concrete Implementation

There is exactly **one** concrete implementation: the unexported `service` struct in the same file:

**`/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/markdown.go`** (line 57-60)

```go
type service struct {
    md goldmark.Markdown
}
```

It wraps the `goldmark` library, configured with GitHub Flavored Markdown plus optional custom extensions for `#tag` and `@mention` syntax.

Additionally, there is a helper struct (not implementing `Service` itself but used by `service.RenderMarkdown` and `service.RenameTag`):

**`/bench/home/work/internal/markdown/renderer/markdown_renderer.go`** -- `MarkdownRenderer` struct, which renders goldmark AST back to markdown text. Instantiated via `renderer.NewMarkdownRenderer()`.

### 3. Where the Implementation Is Constructed/Instantiated

The `Service` is constructed via the `markdown.NewService()` factory function (line 85 of `markdown.go`). It accepts functional options (`WithTagExtension()`, `WithMentionExtension()`).

There are **three** instantiation sites:

| Location | File | Line(s) | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Production** | `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go` | 48-51 | Created inside `NewAPIV1Service()` with both tag and mention extensions enabled, stored as `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` |
| **Test helper** | `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go` | 44-47 | Created for integration tests, injected directly into `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` |
| **Runner (defined but not called)** | `/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` | 19 | `NewRunner()` accepts `markdown.Service` as a parameter but is never actually called in the current codebase -- the `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` free function is used directly instead |

### 4. Which Components Hold References to the Interface

Three structs hold a field of type `markdown.Service`:

**a) `APIV1Service`** -- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go` line 35
```go
MarkdownService markdown.Service
```
This is the primary holder. It uses the service in:
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` lines 108 and 447 -- calls `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, s.MarkdownService)` on memo create and update
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go` line 85 -- calls `s.MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet()` for webhook payload snippets
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go` line 32 -- calls `s.MarkdownService.ExtractAll()` to resolve @mention targets

**b) `RSSService`** -- `/bench/home/work/server/router/rss/rss.go` line 45
```go
MarkdownService markdown.Service
```
Receives its `markdown.Service` from `apiV1Service.MarkdownService` at server startup (`server.go` line 85). Uses it in:
- `rss.go` line 339 -- calls `s.MarkdownService.RenderHTML()` to produce HTML descriptions for RSS feed items

**c) `memopayload.Runner`** -- `/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` line 16
```go
MarkdownService markdown.Service
```
Designed to batch-rebuild memo payloads. Its `NewRunner()` constructor exists but is never called in the current production code. The standalone function `RebuildMemoPayload()` in the same package accepts `markdown.Service` as a parameter and is the entry point actually used.

### Dependency Flow Summary

```
server.NewServer()
  --> apiv1.NewAPIV1Service()
        --> markdown.NewService(WithTagExtension(), WithMentionExtension())
        --> stores it in APIV1Service.MarkdownService
  --> rss.NewRSSService(..., apiV1Service.MarkdownService)
        --> stores it in RSSService.MarkdownService
```

### Frontend (TypeScript) -- No Equivalent Interface

The frontend does **not** define a markdown processing interface/trait. Instead it uses the `react-markdown` library directly via the `MemoMarkdownRenderer` React component at `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/MemoContent/MemoMarkdownRenderer.tsx`. This component configures remark/rehype plugin pipelines inline (remarkGfm, remarkMath, remarkBreaks, custom remarkTag, remarkMention, etc.) and maps HTML elements to custom React components. There is a `MarkdownRenderContext` (React context for tracking nesting depth) and a `ReactMarkdownProps` interface, but neither represents a pluggable markdown processing abstraction.

h13.

**`markdown.Service`** is the interface, defined in `internal/markdown/markdown.go`. It declares methods like `ExtractAll`, `RenderHTML`, `GenerateSnippet`, etc.

**impl** — The single concrete implementation is the unexported `service` struct in the same file (`internal/markdown/markdown.go`), which wraps the `goldmark` library.

**construction** — It is built by the factory function `markdown.NewService()` (also in `internal/markdown/markdown.go`). At runtime, the main construction site is `server/router/api/v1/v1.go` inside `NewAPIV1Service()`, which calls `markdown.NewService(markdown.WithTagExtension(), markdown.WithMentionExtension())`. The resulting instance is then passed to `rss.NewRSSService()` in `server/server.go`.

**holders** — Two components hold the `markdown.Service` interface at runtime:

1. **`APIV1Service`** (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go`, field `MarkdownService`) — uses it for memo create/update payload rebuilding, webhook snippet generation, and @mention extraction.
2. **`RSSService`** (`server/router/rss/rss.go`, field `MarkdownService`) — uses it to call `RenderHTML()` for RSS feed item descriptions.

(A third struct, `memopayload.Runner` in `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`, declares the field but its constructor is never called in production; the standalone `RebuildMemoPayload()` function receives the service as a parameter instead.)
